title: Nsight tiling vs cooperative-kernel sweep: notes and follow-ups
content:
Context:
Quick capture from exploratory profiling of the decoder attention kernel and the KV-cache memcpy/prepare stage. Goal was to compare two implementation strategies that we are considering for the small-batch, variable-length path: (A) tiled kernels with aggressive shared-memory tiling per head, and (B) cooperative-group kernels that shard heads across thread-blocks and use warp-level intrinsics to reduce sharedmem pressure.

Why we ran this:
- Observed low SM residency on CPU-driven small microbatches (2-4 requests) and high tail latency variance.
- Hypothesis: current kernels are limited by either per-block register/sharedmem constraints (reducing occupancy) or by memory bank conflicts when tiling is too aggressive. Cooperative kernels might trade less sharedmem for more warp-aggregation, increasing occupancy.

Experiment setup (notes):
- Model: transformer-decoder, 6 layers, 32 heads, 64-dim head (toy model but kernel is representative).
- Hardware: p4d.24xlarge equivalent (A100-like); single GPU used during capture.
- Runtime: local branch w/ cudaGraph capture enabled, dynamic KV cache.
- Captures: Nsight Systems timeline (.nsys) + Nsight Compute sampling for hot kernels.
- Commands (approx):
  - nsys profile --trace=nvtx,cuda,nvtx-api --output=tiling-sweep-2023-07 ./run_inference --batch=3 --seq=512
  - ncu --target-processes all -k attention_tiled -k attention_coop --set full -o ncu-tiling.csv ./run_inference ...

What we saw (high-level):
- Kernel-level occupancy numbers (Nsight Compute):
  - attention_tiled (current prod-like): active_warps_per_sm ~ 10/64 -> ~15% theoretical occupancy; registers/block 256, sharedmem/block 48KB (near limit). Tensor-core math intensive but low utilization (~18%).
  - attention_coop (cooperative experiment): active_warps_per_sm ~ 28/64 -> ~44% occupancy; registers/block lowered to 160, sharedmem/block ~24KB. Tensor-core utilization improved to ~36% in sustained phases.

- Stall and reason breakdown (sampled):
  - attention_tiled: majority stall due to memory dependency (DRAM) ~38%, then serialization due to long-latency sharedmem bank conflicts ~22%, instruction fetch/dispatch ~12%.
  - attention_coop: stalls shift toward pipeline busy/memory pipeline ~28%, but bank-conflict fraction drops to single digits. L2 read-hit-rate slightly higher (2-3%) probably due to cooperative aggregation creating improved locality.

- CUDA Graph interaction:
  - When running under cudaGraph capture, attention_tiled showed slightly higher variance in kernel launch spacing (micro gaps between graph nodes) — suspect capture serialization + uneven block execution times leading to host-side gaps.
  - attention_coop produced more uniform kernel durations across repeats; graph replay latency reduced 6-9ms on the test trace.

- Timeline observations (Nsight Systems):
  - Several small memcpyAsync -> kernel launches were interleaved with short idle pockets on the GPU. These pockets line up with host-thread wake jitter (we were still using a non-pin thread for the capture process in this run).
  - In tiled variant, per-layer kernel completion had high variance across SMs causing staggered stream activity; cooperative variant showed tighter completion alignment.

Detailed micro-notes / snippets (raw):
- Attention tiled: appears to do more per-thread work (more registers). Compiler unroll blows up register pressure when we try to vectorize head loops. Tried smaller unroll and saw occupancy go from 15% -> 28% but instruction count increased and time didn't net improve.
- Cooperative: using cooperative groups + ballot/warp intrinsics to reduce per-thread register footprint. Need to be careful with synchronizations; found a mis-sync in the first implementation that caused occasional nondeterministic values at tail positions. Fixed by moving a barrier and revalidating against reference.
- Sharedmem: bank conflicts were reproducible when sequence length % tile_size == edge case (e.g., 128 mod 32 patterns). Remapping tile stride fixed conflict but changed memory access pattern affecting L2 prefetcher.

Hypotheses / interpretations: 
1) The dominant limiter for small microbatches is occupancy (register/sharedmem constraints) rather than pure compute. Raising occupancy improves sustained tensor-core utilization and reduces tail variance.
2) Tiling optimized for single large sequence length is brittle across distribution; cooperative approach generalizes better for mixed length workloads.
3) CUDA Graph capture can amplify small kernel-duration skews; more uniform kernel execution time reduces replay jitter.

Quick perf numbers (median of 20 runs, toy model):
- tiled: avg latency 43.5ms, p95 72ms, GPU-active-time per request 28ms
- coop:  avg latency 37.8ms, p95 49ms, GPU-active-time per request 22ms
- delta: ~13% med latency improvement, ~32% p95 improvement on this workload

Open questions / follow-ups: 
- Re-run with pinned host threads + cpu affinity to eliminate host-side wake jitter. Current capture used default Linux scheduling.
- Sweep register limits with -maxrregcount and compile-time tiling parameters to see Pareto of occupancy vs instruction count.
- Validate on longer sequences (2048) and on smaller GPUs (e.g., V100/30xx-class) to check portability of occupancy gains.
- Measure end-to-end effect in cudaGraph with real DAG (multi-kernel per layer including fused-project/fused-softmax). Does cooperative approach still win when combined with other fused kernels?
- Investigate L2 prefetch behaviour observed (slight bump in hit-rate). Could be beneficial; measure streaming read pattern and see if caching triggers more coalesced loads.

Action items (short):
- [Priya] Create systematic compile matrix: tiling sizes {16,32,64}, unroll {1,2}, reg cap {max,220,180} and run ncu baseline. Target date: 2023-08-09.
- [Ethan] Re-run Nsight Systems with pinned host threads and capture host-side scheduling metrics. Target: 2023-07-21.
- [Mina] Add unit test comparing outputs for 1% error tolerance across implementations (determinism check). Target: 2023-07-28.
- [ENG] Triage the nondet barrier bug and include small reproducer in repo as an integration test.

Notes to self / miscellaneous: 
- Keep a copy of the ncu cmdline flags used in the captures; subtle differences in sampling granularity change the observed stall distributions.
- When exporting Nsight timelines to csv, filter by stream id to remove host-side sample noise.

References / links (local):
- PR with coop kernel prototype: github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/723
- Jira ticket tracking rollout risk: JIRA-ENG-1842

Summary (one-line): cooperative-group kernel prototype increases SM occupancy and tensor-core utilization on small microbatches, reduces tail latency and cudaGraph replay jitter; follow-up is a controlled compile-time sweep and multi-hardware validation before moving to staging.
